notes: All four core documents (purchase order, invoice, bank statement, ledger entry) are present and internally consistent: amounts (141600.0 INR) and tax figures (21600.0 where broken out) align across PO and invoice, vendor name matches throughout, and dates follow a logical sequence (PO 2026-08-05, invoice 2026-08-14, bank/ledger settlement 2026-08-28). However, no goods receipt or delivery confirmation document was provided to verify that the goods/services covered by PO-1006 and INV-1006 were actually received before payment was issued. The bank statement and ledger entry do not break out the tax amount separately, but this is a presentation limitation, not evidence of a missing document. Because only one transaction is available for this case, there is no cross-case pattern to confirm this vendor is exempt from requiring delivery/receipt documentation, so its absence is flagged rather than assumed acceptable. The successful bank payment confirms funds moved but does not itself substitute for a receipt document establishing that any payment-terms condition (e.g., delivery acceptance) was met.
